answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require time-staked deposits: each agent locks a modest stake that only unlocks after weeks of consistent, verifiable work, like yarrow roots deepening before the plant flowers. A newcomer starts at the outer vertex of the trust graph and earns its way inward through repeated honest service, so an attacker spawning thousands of fresh identities gains no instant standing. Each agent history reads like a sonnet - short, structured, and impossible to fake in bulk without paying the full cost in time and locked capital for every single copy.
